To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of multiple local cues in a globalization framework based upon spectral clustering yields state of the art performance in contour detection, and that the output of any good contour detector can be converted into a hierarchical region graph by means of a generic segmentation algorithm.

(1) the output of a contour detector can be transformed into a hierarchical region segmentation; and (2) the output of the segmentation algorithm is a hierarchy of segmentations, each of which can be refined by user annotations.
(i) the output of our contour detector can be used as input to our region tree construction algorithm, and (ii) this region tree construction algorithm can be used to segment images.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two key issues in computer vision: (i) how to automatically generate a hierarchy of contours from images, and (ii) how to use such a hierarchy to segment an image into regions of similar appearance.
